issues.description: In the template implementation of simulate_msd_two_rounds (template/msd.py) the Stim Circuit is constructed with an unexpected argument: circ = stim.Circuit(p). The Stim Circuit constructor used throughout the solution and elsewhere in the repository is called with no arguments (circ = stim.Circuit()). Passing a float parameter to stim.Circuit in the template is inconsistent with the solution and will cause confusion or runtime errors when students run or adapt the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor call in the template to use no arguments: replace circ = stim.Circuit(p) with circ = stim.Circuit(). This matches the solution and avoids passing an unexpected parameter. Add a short comment in the template explaining that Stim Circuit takes no positional parameters to prevent similar confusion.

issues.description: The function correct_teleportation is declared (problem statement and template) as correct_teleportation(teleportation_measurements, x_measurements). In the solution, call sites pass the destructive X measurements (final measurements) as the first argument and the teleportation measurements as the second argument (e.g., correct_teleportation(measurements[:, final], measurements[:, tele]) at solution/msd.py). This reverses the documented parameter order. The implementation in the solution uses a symmetric XOR so it functions despite the reversed order, but the mismatch between signature/documentation and call sites is confusing and may mislead students about the expected shapes/origins of the two arrays.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter order consistent and explicit across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either (A) change the documented signature and template docstring to match how the solution calls the function (i.e., first argument = final/destructive X measurements, second = teleportation measurements) and add an example showing expected shapes/sources of the arrays, or (B) update the solution call sites to pass arguments in the documented order. Also expand the docstring to state which axis corresponds to shots vs. measurement indices to remove ambiguity.
